Picked up adhesive from supply house. Drove to site. Checked in with customer. Brought tools to roof. Found the insulation hanging from roof. Reattached insulation using adhesive. Checked unit for spots that looked like it could leak. Took off all the panels on unit. Checked for spots that could leak through gaskets. Did not find anything. There was water on the fan section floor. Checked the economizer section. Did not find anything that stood out. Went into condensing section to see if I could find something. Found an open hole where piping could have been but wasn't covered. After speaking with Role, I taped up the hole. If leak continues, will water unit to find leak. Explained findings to customer. Customer agreed. Checked out with customer.

Found hot gas line cracked at discharge header. Will need to be rewelded and new drier installed and evacuate then charged with 47# of R 410a.     Repair crack in hot gas line stub and evacuate to 500 microns. Add 40# of R410 A to circuit A.

Arrived at site and gained roof access. Isolated power to unit. Pressurized and leak checked circuit A. Located leak at hot gas bypass line weld. Used torch to repair leak. Replaced liquid line filter drier core. Put circuit in vacuum and charged with 29.4 lbs of 410a. Checked operations upon completion. All okay @ this time.
DOA - BROKEN HIGH PRESSURE SWITCH
Completed the trouble shooting of the unit found bad high pressure control need new control also completed the start up of all units

Arrived. Checked in with customer. Located RTU. Unbuttoned panels. Current alarms t051, t052, which are A1, A2 compressor failures. Supply fan running upon arrival. Circuit A circuit breaker good. Power to compressor contractors good. 480, 280v. Examined circuit piping. Found one of the two HPS wires completely detached from HPS. Cleared alarms. Attempted to start compressors in service test to no avail. Generated same alarms. Pressures equal at 190#. Refrigerant temperatures equal at 66 degrees. Powered machine off. Verified 0v. Repaired wire at HPS. Powered on. Ran both compressors in service test. Amp draws good. Pressures good. Circuit A is operational at this time. However, this is not a long term solution. CCS will need to properly replace HPS by pulling 410a, replacing switch, pulling vacuum and charging circuit. There is power at RTU when RTU is on. There is not power to RTU when RTU is off. Had Phil order HPS. Will schedule time to make repair. Circuit A ran under its own control during my visit. Supply fan running upon departure. Buttoned up all panels. Cleaned up work area. Checked out with customer.
Old Compressor Grounded. Replaced Old Compressor With New

Checked in. Gained access to ground mounted rooftop unit. Found combustion blowers operating. Heating locked out. Opened panels. Found rollout switch lockout fault. Reset lockout safety. Started heating. Monitored operation. Found first few burners not firing correctly. Shut down unit. Removed and inspected burners and firebox access panel. All okay. Found leaking seal by burner. Sealed leak. Restarted unit. Reinstalled burners and panels. Restarted unit. Restarted heating. Checked operation. Okay now. Cycled unit several times. All okay. Closed and secured panels. Checked out air handler on F building also. Reset high limit. Okay now. checked out.

3/23/17 Drove to site,and checked in. Repaired furnace compartment access door. Found that draft inducing fan exhaust duct does not line up with access door. Disassembled unit to find out why access door does not line up with draft inducing fan motor ductwork. Found that heat exchanger is incorrectly supported on one and just causing the whole assembly to be out of level and out of alignment. Spoke with Allen Henderson in warrantee department about situation was told to take pictures and send them to him. Reassembled unit and disabled furnace section until repairs can be made.
